title: Step 1: The Great Disappearance
text: Imagine waking up one morning to find that all the bees in the world have suddenly disappeared. No more buzzing, no more honey. At first, it might seem like a small change. But within a few months, supermarkets would run out of apples, almonds, and tomatoes. Why? Because nature works in a delicate balance, and every creature, no matter how small, plays a crucial role.

title: Step 2: What If...?
text: Why do you think the disappearance of bees would affect the apples we eat? If a tiny insect vanishes, how does it connect to our dinner plates? What would happen if a single species went extinct?

content.title: Step 3: The Invisible Threads
content.description: Watch how energy and life flow from the sun, to the plants, to the animals, and back to the earth in a continuous cycle.

title: Step 4: Ecosystems and Interdependence
text: The connection you just saw is called an Ecosystem. An ecosystem is a community of living organisms (plants, animals, microbes) interacting with non-living things (water, air, soil) in their environment. In nature, organisms depend on each other for survival. This is called Interdependence. For example, bees help pollinate apple flowers, which then turn into apples.

content.definition_preview: A community of interacting organisms and their physical environment.
The dependence of two or more things on each other.

content.question: Which of the following is the best example of interdependence in an ecosystem?
options: A rock sitting in a river.
A cloud raining on a mountain.
A piece of plastic floating in the ocean.

title: Step 6: Think About It
text: Explain in your own words how a lion depends on grass, even though lions only eat meat. How would you explain this connection to a younger friend or sibling?

title: Step 7: Connecting the Dots
text: This idea of interdependence connects to what you learned about Food Chains. But it goes further—it affects human agriculture, weather patterns, and even global warming. Every action in nature has a reaction.

content.title: Step 8: The Web of Life Challenge
content.description: Draw a food web for a forest near you. Include at least 5 organisms and draw arrows showing who eats whom. What happens if you cross out one organism from your web?
